subject: English
central_question: How do travel and adventure develop curiosity, courage, friendship, endurance and awareness of the natural and human world?
in_scope_units: The Tunnel—Suraj's fascination with the railway, jungle and tunnel.
The steam engine as a sensory image and the contrast between machine and forest.
Sunder Singh's work as watchman and friendship with Suraj.
The leopard incident, courage, responsibility and railway safety.
Sound words, simile, personification, imagery and description.
Travel—the speaker's fascination with distant trains.
Rhyme scheme, repetition, imagery, sound, tone and symbolism.
Train vocabulary, diamante poetry and descriptive journey writing.
Conquering the Summit—Arunima Sinha's goal, preparation and achievement.
Bachendri Pal's encouragement and the importance of mental strength.
Seven Summits, Mount Vinson, endurance and resilience.
Adventure-sport viewpoints, risk, equipment, training and supervision.
School-trip announcement listening and responsible preparation.
banned_topics: Technical railway engineering or tunnel construction.
Instructions for dangerous adventure sports without supervision.
External records or dates not contained in the source.

known_pitfalls.claim: Suraj enters the tunnel to damage the train.
known_pitfalls.correction: He explores from curiosity and later helps protect the line.

known_pitfalls.claim: The leopard is simply a villain.
known_pitfalls.correction: It belongs to the jungle; danger arises where animal habitat and railway meet.

known_pitfalls.claim: The speaker in Travel dislikes current friends.
known_pitfalls.correction: The speaker values friends but also desires new journeys.

known_pitfalls.claim: Arunima succeeds through physical strength alone.
known_pitfalls.correction: The text stresses preparation, mentorship, determination and mental endurance.
The unit stresses training, equipment, supervision and judgement.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with Suraj's sensory experience of the tunnel.
Analyse friendship, the leopard and responsibility.
Use Travel for imagery, repetition and symbolism.
Use Conquering the Summit for endurance and mentorship.
End with descriptive writing, listening and balanced adventure discussion.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The unit provides comprehension, extract-based reflection, vocabulary, poetry, listening, speaking, descriptive writing and adventure-sport activities.
